summary: @servicetitan/cp-react-hooks preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, marks it executable, and immediately runs it against math_init.js — a 727KB Bun-only CJS bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) shipped at the tarball root that is heavily obfuscated (rotated string-array via a `WV8StW` rotator over a large numeric constants table, hex-mangled identifiers `_0xNNNN`, `MmgoCP` etc.). The bundle is invoked only through the freshly downloaded Bun binary rather than Node, so its behavior is not observable to Node-based tooling. The package presents itself as a ServiceTitan `CustomerPortal react hooks` library, with small plausible hook files under dist/ acting as camouflage; math_init.js is not referenced from dist/index.js and has no relation to a React-hooks library's declared purpose. The preinstall lifecycle hook fires on `npm install` before any code review, and the executed payload is opaque, unpinned in behavior, and unrelated to the advertised functionality.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
